name: TAURUS
question: What are the 12-month safety and symptom outcomes of mirabegron compared with tolterodine ER in adults with overactive bladder?

design.population: Adults with overactive bladder symptoms for at least 3 months, at least eight daily micturitions, and at least three urgency episodes in a 3-day diary; 81.3% of treated patients had participated in previous phase 3 studies.
design.description: Multicenter, double-blind, active-controlled randomized safety trial
design.locator: Full text, Fig. 2 and Methods, pp 297–298

verdictNote: Safety was assessed descriptively, without a reported comparative hypothesis test.
takeaway: Over 12 months, mirabegron 50 mg and 100 mg had treatment-emergent adverse events in 485/812 (59.7%) and 503/820 (61.3%) treated patients, versus 508/812 (62.6%) with tolterodine ER 4 mg. No comparative safety hypothesis test was reported.

reports.label: 12-month safety and efficacy
reports.citation: Chapple CR, Kaplan SA, Mitcheson D, et al. "Randomized Double-blind, Active-controlled Phase 3 Study to Assess 12-Month Safety and Efficacy of Mirabegron, a β3-Adrenoceptor Agonist, in Overactive Bladder." *Eur Urol.* 2013;63(2):296-305. doi:10.1016/j.eururo.2012.10.048

results.measure: Patients with at least one treatment-emergent adverse event over 12 months
results.note: Primary safety variable in the safety analysis set (all randomized patients who took at least one dose); no formal sample-size calculation or comparative safety hypothesis test was reported.
results.locator: Full text, Methods, pp 297–298; Table 2, p 299

results.measure: Adjusted mean change from baseline to final visit, mm Hg
results.note: Safety analysis set (812, 820, 812); adjusted mean changes with arm-specific 95% CIs; final visit used last observation carried forward. No between-arm estimate or P value was reported.
results.locator: Full text, Appendix 5, p 304; Statistical analysis, p 298

results.measure: Adjusted mean change in micturitions per 24 hours from baseline to final visit
results.note: Secondary efficacy measure; numerical improvement began at month 1 and persisted through month 12. Final-visit analysis used last observation carried forward; no formal between-arm efficacy comparison was performed.
results.locator: Full text, Efficacy assessments, pp 300–301; Statistical analysis, p 298

results.measure: Adjusted mean change in incontinence episodes per 24 hours from baseline to final visit
results.note: FAS-I comprised FAS patients with at least one baseline incontinence episode; no formal between-arm efficacy comparison was performed.
results.locator: Full text, Statistical analysis, p 298; Table 1, p 298; Efficacy assessments, p 300

harms.label: Hypertension
harms.note: Treatment-emergent adverse event (MedDRA preferred term) in the safety analysis set.

harms.label: Urinary tract infection
harms.note: Treatment-emergent adverse event in the safety analysis set.

harms.label: Urinary retention
harms.locator: Full text, Safety assessments and Table 2, p 299
harms.note: Acute urinary retention occurred in 0, 1, and 1 patients, respectively; the latter two required catheterization. No serious urinary-retention adverse event was reported.

harms.label: Discontinuation due to adverse events
harms.note: Disposition denominators are randomized patients; safety analysis denominators differ.

delivery.label: Run-in and assigned treatment
delivery.value: Two-week single-blind placebo run-in, then once-daily double-blind mirabegron 50 mg, mirabegron 100 mg, or tolterodine ER 4 mg for 12 months. Compliance was assessed by pill count at each visit; 80–120% of prescribed doses defined compliance.
delivery.locator: Full text, Patients and study design, p 297

relations.note: Some entrants previously completed SCORPIO; TAURUS assessed safety during a new 12-month treatment course.
